gaps.sentence: The magazine ___ the politician's words, which caused a scandal (QUOTE).
gaps.hint: quoted wrongly — that is why there was a scandal (mis-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix mis- means wrongly: misquoted explains the scandal. The past tense is needed.

gaps.sentence: There are many ___ (SIMILAR) between the two languages.
gaps.explanation: 'Many' needs a plural countable noun: similarities (note the -ty to -ties spelling).

gaps.sentence: The ___ (DEEP) of the lake is still unknown.
I'm afraid your passport is ___ — it expired last month (VALID).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: it has expired
gaps.explanation: An expired document is invalid (in- + valid); an adjective is needed after 'is'.

gaps.sentence: The company is a major ___ (EMPLOY) in the region.
gaps.hint: the company gives jobs — it is the one who employs
gaps.explanation: An employer gives work; an employee receives it. The sentence is about the company.

gaps.sentence: He is under a lot of ___ at work (PRESS).
gaps.hint: noun needed after 'a lot of'; fixed phrase 'under ___'
gaps.explanation: 'Under pressure' is the fixed phrase; the noun of 'press' is 'pressure'.

gaps.sentence: New technology has ___ the way we work (REVOLUTION).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ise forms the verb: revolutionise. After 'has' the past participle 'revolutionised' is needed.

gaps.sentence: The street market sells ___ fruit in summer (JUICE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -y forms the adjective: juicy fruit. A comparative or adverb cannot modify 'fruit'.
